messages:
Maria Chen: Hey team — quick sync on the console slab idea. thinking of a small ‘workbench’ panel per-route that surfaces routing hints, quota peek, and quick model swap.

Kevin Patel: +1 to a compact panel. main ask: make it non-blocking and hideable. people want a lightweight glance, not a full modal. :eyes:

Raz Kline: agree. also want telemetry links from the slab directly into the detailed route timeline. one click to jump to trace.

Anna Gómez: can we show per-model token burn estimate for the last 10k requests? a tiny sparkline would help.

Maria Chen: yes — sparkline + avg latency + quota remaining. but need to be careful about sampling. we shouldn't hammer the metrics APIs for every open panel.

Kevin Patel: sampling = important. proposal: panel fetches cached summary endpoint: `/api/console/summary?route_id=XXX&window=10m` which returns pre-aggregated fields. cache TTL 30s.

Raz Kline: that cache TTL sounds right. for rollouts we also need an indicator of active variant and fallback policy. show current variant id and % traffic.

Anna Gómez: UX question: where does saved query/filter live — inside slab or global views? users sometimes want route-specific presets.

Maria Chen: slab should offer two buttons: `Apply route-presets` and `Open global views`. route-presets are namespaced by route id. global views are cross-route.

Kevin Patel: internal API needs to support that: `POST /api/console/apply_view` with body `{ "view_id": "v123", "scope": "route" }` and the server resolves and returns an adapted query. we should version that contract.

Raz Kline: one more contract detail: when applying route-presets we must also return a `cost_estimate` object so UI can show token burn delta pre/post. example response snippet:```{ "applied_query": "...", "cost_delta": "+2.1%" }```

Anna Gómez: love the cost delta. make sure it surfaces a tooltip explaining the baseline calculation. ppl will ask how it’s computed.

Maria Chen: rollout UX: the slab will highlight if route is in canary and provide a one-click `override to safe` that routes traffic to fallback model. need guardrails (confirm modal).

Kevin Patel: backend must implement `POST /api/route/override` with authz check. ops-bot should post to channel on successful override.

ops-bot: [SYSTEM] deploy-watch: override event recorded for route rt-42 by Kevin. link: https://internal/overrides/rt-42

Raz Kline: about telemetry links — include `open-in-trace` with context params: route, model_variant, sample_id. that makes reproducing failures easier.

Anna Gómez: small UI nit: compact slab should collapse to an icon that shows a hovercard with two quick actions: switch model, open telemetry. keeps console tidy.

Maria Chen: accessibility note: keyboard shortcuts to open slab and toggle favorite views. track that in the product PRD.

Kevin Patel: edge case: user applies a route-preset that references a model not deployed in the region. UI should show a toast and a `show compatible` dropdown with nearest alternatives.

Raz Kline: decision: we wire the slab to the summary API, the view-apply API, and a separate override API. telemetry links are deep links — no heavy payloads. implement feature flag `feat/console-slab` for progressive rollout.

Anna Gómez: rollout plan: alpha to internal, beta to customers with opt-in, then GA. keep metrics for adoption and error rate.

Maria Chen: who owns the API schema? Raz + Kevin to draft. Anna to mock quick UI. I'll write the alpha checklist.

Kevin Patel: will draft schemas and add examples in the API docs. ping me for review.

Raz Kline: ok starting a PR: `console/summary-api` + `console/view-apply`. will link tests.

Anna Gómez: I'll post screenshots in #product-demo when ready.

Maria Chen: thanks — feel free to @me for any blocking decisions. :thumbsup:
